explanation: Use a one-row dynamic program. Each cell's path count is its previous-row count plus its left neighbor's current-row count; the first row and column each have one path.
timeComplexity: O(m times n) time for an m by n grid.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Every path to an interior cell arrives either from above or from the left, and these possibilities are disjoint. Summing those predecessor counts therefore counts every allowed path once. The one-row table retains the previous-row count until it is combined with the already updated left neighbor.
walkthrough: In a 2-by-5 grid, a complete route contains four right moves and one down move. The down move can occupy any of the five move positions, giving 5 unique paths. The dynamic program returns the same count.
edgeCases: A one-row or one-column grid has one path.
Only right and down moves are allowed.
Dimensions are positive and the returned count fits the advertised int contract.
